entities.rationale: Rich and well governed, so collapse is mostly global doom plus nuclear-state war risk; abundance needs essentials to fall from 24% to under 10% of income, which an aging population's health bill makes unlikely without superintelligence.
Nuclear power and food self-sufficiency make it resilient, but weaker political stability and rising debt add risk; 27% essentials cost means near-free needs superintelligence-driven deflation.

Severe water stress, a fragile power grid, very high violence and weak state capacity make prolonged loss of an essential a real risk; abundance is remote without broad, well-distributed superintelligence gains.

Heavy energy import dependence, high debt and one of the steepest aging curves strain the system, though it starts from full access; extreme aging keeps health costs far above a near-free level without superintelligence.

A third of people are already undernourished and climate vulnerability is high, so drought-driven food loss is the main path to collapse; abundance would require both superintelligence and fast diffusion to a low-income economy.
Ample water and energy, but armed groups, high homicide and low political stability make a renewed security breakdown the dominant risk; middle income keeps strict abundance unlikely.
Highly capable state and tech base well placed to capture superintelligence gains, offset by North Korean war risk, 83% energy imports and the world's most extreme aging.

Peaceful and rich, but water stress heading toward extreme levels and heavy energy imports are its weak points; strong solar potential helps, yet aging keeps essentials far above 10% of income without superintelligence.

A food and energy exporter that is physically secure, but repeated economic crises and modest state effectiveness threaten health and security services and limit how much superintelligence wealth reaches everyone.
Energy and water surpluses, strong institutions and geographic safety leave little beyond global doom; strict abundance depends almost entirely on superintelligence collapsing health and other costs.

Nearly five years of full-scale war with strikes on the grid already put security and energy at the edge of the collapse threshold, and renewed Russian aggression is plausible later; abundance needs both lasting peace and superintelligence.

Rich and fiscally strong, but water depends on energy-hungry desalination, food is imported, extreme heat rises and regional war risk is real; heavy defense spending also counts against near-free security.
Stable and growing fast, but as NATO's frontline with Russia it carries above-average war risk, and steep aging pushes health costs up; abundance hinges on superintelligence.
A food and energy exporter with strong institutions and isolation from most wars; drought and heat are the main local stresses, and near-free essentials require superintelligence.
Very wealthy with low debt and world-class flood defenses, but sea-level rise and 88% energy imports are long-run vulnerabilities; strict abundance needs superintelligence.

Clean domestic power, abundant water, low debt and top-tier governance leave mainly global doom and Baltic security risk; it is among the likeliest to reach near-free essentials if superintelligence delivers.

The richest and most energy-secure country here, with essentials already at 20% of income and a sovereign fund buffer, so collapse is near the global floor and abundance is likelier than anywhere else listed.
